question:
A 23-year-old Caucasian male presents to the emergency department with a persistent penile erection for the last 6 hours. He recently began outpatient treatment for depression with associated insomnia. He traveled to Mexico 5 months ago. His medical history is otherwise unremarkable.

Which of the following is the most likely precipitating factor for priapism in this patient?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Depression treatment with bupropion -> potential side effect of priapism -> 60% CHAIN: Depression treatment with venlafaxine -> less commonly associated with priapism compared to trazodone -> 70% CHAIN: Depression treatment with trazodone -> known association with priapism -> 90% CHAIN: Sickle cell disease -> can predispose to priapism due to impaired blood flow regulation -> 80% CHAIN: Infection acquired in Mexico -> unlikely to directly cause priapism -> 60%
analysis: The most likely precipitating factor for priapism in this patient is the depression treatment with trazodone, which is known to be associated with priapism as a side effect.
